doc.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Pay for arranging on Maynard's band; arranger versus orchestrator
summary: With Maynard he was paid only about a hundred dollars if a chart was recorded; he re-scored Newport Youth Band pieces; arranger versus orchestrator scale.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How do you determine — obviously it would change over the years — but what you get paid for your writing?

Well that’s funny. With Maynard’s band — well let me just go back a step for a second. When I was on the Newport Youth Band we had I think it was an octet or a nonette with Ronnie Cuber, Eddie Gomez and guys. And I wrote this whole book. And when I got on Maynard’s band I re-scored four or five of those things for the band: “Green Dolphin Street,” “Whisper Not,” “Airegin,” some things that became good staple things for Maynard over the years. But with Maynard’s band, you didn’t get paid. You copied, you wrote, and you didn’t really care because you figured you have a band that was playing your music. You got paid if it was recorded. And then the company paid something like a hundred bucks or something like that. So it wasn’t a thrilling amount of money but the fact is you were getting your music played all the time. So at that point in time that’s fine. Then you start realizing, as you start working for other bands in other situations that there’s a price. You try — each arranger, from a Local, from a musician’s point of view I believe — now my wife is good at this because she’s really the manager of all this stuff. There is no such thing as an arranger’s scale. There is an orchestration scale, and it’s two different things. Okay? The arranger is the guy who sort of like puts — if I give you a sheet and I give you lead lines and say here, now French horns play here, trumpets play here, the orchestrator kind of takes that and fills in the missing — to me it’s always been ©Fillius Jazz Archive -7-
one thing. Because and a lot of movie writers and a lot of guys don’t do their own orchestrating.
They write the skeleton kind of?
